land.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt up to Herakleopolis, the lands the Piye page says his authority reached after his campaign (Thebes, the western oases and Herakleopolis)

predecessors.note: Third Intermediate Period page: the Twenty-third was the "Upper Egyptian Libyan" dynasty, capital Heracleopolis Magna. Cliopatria's Twenty-second and Twenty-third Dynasty rows for -800..-701 are reviewed by me-03-b as wrong.

land.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis, taken by Shebitku "around 712 BC" (25th Dynasty page)
the eastern Delta around Tanis, where Osorkon IV and the other Delta kings submitted to Piye

predecessors.note: The Delta kinglets are drawn as vassals 728-712, then ruled directly.

land.text: The Napatan kingdom whose kings became pharaohs; its Nubian land stays with kingdom-of-kush, this dossier covers the Egyptian realm only
Thebes and Upper Egypt, which "peacefully submitted itself to Psamtik's fleet in 656 BC"

successors.note: Lower Egypt had passed to the Assyrian-backed Saite kings in 663. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Slug changed from twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt: in 656 Psamtik I was Assyria's vassal (assyrian-egypt); the Twenty-sixth Dynasty dossier begins in 655.

land.text: "The 25th Dynasty ended with its rulers retreating to their spiritual homeland at Napata"

capitals.name: Napata (Jebel Barkal)
capitals.note: Infobox lists Napata and Memphis together as capital; Napata was the Kushite royal seat (the Piye page has him ruling Nubia and Upper Egypt from Napata).

capitals.name: Memphis
capitals.note: The page says Shebitku moved the capital to Memphis after conquering Lower Egypt (around 712); it also says Shabaka "transferred the capital to Memphis" and that Taharqa was crowned at Memphis and ruled from Tanis (690). Memphis was lost to Esarhaddon in 671-669 and 667.

capitals.name: Thebes (Luxor)
capitals.note: Tantamani fled to Thebes in 663 and Kushite authority in Upper Egypt lasted to 656 (Assyrian conquest page); the page names no capital for these years, so this is the researcher's reading.

rulers.name: Piye
rulers.note: Infobox table c. 747-714; the lead and the Piye page give 744-714; the Victory Stele page 747-716.

rulers.name: Shebitku
rulers.note: The page says newer evidence indicates "Shabaka ruled after Shebitku, not before"; the infobox table has Shebitku 714-705 and Shabaka 705-690, followed here.

correction.text: Elephantine (Aswan): the southern end of Egypt, where a stela of Kashta was found; Thebes is left out because the 25th page says he "did not control it"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for the Kushite dynasty before -700, and then folds it into Kingdom of Kush). Infobox "Established: 754 BC"; a stela of Kashta was found at Elephantine and his daughter Amenirdis I was adopted as Divine Adoratrice of Amun (Third Intermediate Period page: Kashta "had already extended his kingdom's influence into Thebes"). The 25th page doubts real control, so only a small core is drawn. No infobox area. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Luxor radius removed from the correction (page: Kashta did not control Thebes); Thebes stays with the Twenty-third Dynasty until Piye's gain of 728.

correction.text: Upper Egypt to Herakleopolis: the Piye page says his authority extended north only to Thebes, the western oases and Herakleopolis

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after Piye's campaign of his regnal year 20. The Delta kings submitted but stayed in place (vassal tint, ledger 728-712); Piye went home to Nubia, "never to return to Egypt". Cliopatria's Kingdom of Kush shape for -700..-676 (563,237 km2, bbox to 31.7 N) draws all Egypt, which fits only 712 onward. No infobox area.

correction.text: the whole Nile Valley from the Delta to the south, which the 25th Dynasty page says Shebitku conquered "around 712 BC"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the reunited valley, "as large as it had been since the New Kingdom" (Third Intermediate Period page). Cliopatria draws this only for -700..-676 inside the Kush row (563,237 km2 with Nubia). The Egyptian valley and delta alone is about 121,000 km2 by the gazetteer, plus the desert fringe the dynasty claimed; no infobox area to compare.

correction.text: Upper and Middle Egypt only: Esarhaddon took and sacked Memphis in 671 and Taharqa fled south

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Lower Egypt lost for two years. Assyrian conquest page: in 671 Esarhaddon took Memphis, Taharqa escaped south and Necho I was installed at Sais; the Kushites hold the south.

correction.text: the Nile Valley again: Taharqa reoccupied Memphis and the Delta in 669

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Taharqa's return in 669, when the Assyrian governors fled, before Esarhaddon's death.

correction.text: Upper and Middle Egypt: Ashurbanipal defeated Taharqa in 667 and he fled to Thebes

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 667, Ashurbanipal's army advanced as far south as Thebes; by 665 the rulers of Sais, Mendes and Pelusium still courted Taharqa and Necho I was reinstated as vassal. The Assyrian page also lists Upper Egypt as lost to Ashurbanipal in 667 but then says Kushite authority there persisted until 656; the latter is followed.

correction.text: the Nile Valley as far as Memphis, regained by Tantamani in 664

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Tantamani was ritually installed at Thebes and regained Egypt as far as Memphis, killing Necho I (25th page). The Assyrian page narrates the same return under 663; the 25th page's reign table starts him in 664.

correction.text: Upper Egypt around Thebes, where Kushite authority persisted until Psamtik I's fleet came in 656 (Assyrian conquest page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Thebes was sacked in 663 and Psamtik I took Lower Egypt, Kushite authority in Upper Egypt persisted until 656 (Assyrian conquest page). The extent between Thebes and Herakleopolis in these years is not given by the pages.

region.text: Elephantine (Aswan), where a stela of Kashta was found; Thebes is not drawn, the 25th page saying he influenced it "although he did not control it"

ledger.note: 754: the Kushite Twenty-fifth Dynasty is established, with its reach at Thebes. The infobox says Established 754 BC (the lead gives 744 and the body 747); Kashta "likely exercised some influence" at Thebes, a stela of his stands at Elephantine and his daughter Amenirdis I was adopted as Divine Adoratrice of Amun. The region is the researcher's reading of that influence. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Thebes (Luxor 60 km) removed from the region: the 25th page says Kashta "likely exercised some influence at Thebes (although he did not control it)", and me-03-b's Twenty-third Dynasty holds Thebes until 728.

728: Piye marches on Egypt. The Victory Stele page says Piye "invaded Egypt again in his twentieth regnal year" (reign "circa 747–716" there, so about 728; the Piye page, reign 744–714, gives about 725; the Third Intermediate Period page says c. 732). Tefnakht had besieged Herakleopolis; Piye won "complete victory at Herakleopolis", took Hermopolis after a siege of five months and "capture Memphis after facing strong resistance" (Victory Stele page).

region.text: Thebes, the western oases and the valley to Herakleopolis

ledger.note: 728: Piye holds Upper Egypt to Herakleopolis. The Piye page says he visited Thebes for the Opet Festival, which shows he controlled Upper Egypt by then, and that his authority extended north only to Thebes, the western oases and Herakleopolis; Nimlot of Hermopolis went over to his side. me-03-b's Twenty-third Dynasty dossier carries the matching loss to Kush at 728.

region.text: the Nile Delta under Tefnakht of Sais and the other Delta kings

ledger.note: 728: the Delta kings submit to Piye. The Piye page says he "received the submission of the kings of the Nile Delta", Iuput II of Leontopolis and Osorkon IV of Tanis among them; the Victory Stele page has "Tefnakhte submits to Piye", though the Piye page adds he "refused to personally pay homage to the Kushite ruler". The kings keep their thrones, so the Delta is a tint, not territory.
728: Piye sails south and goes home to Nubia, "never to return to Egypt" (Piye page); the fighting of his campaign ends and the Delta kings are left to rule.

region.text: Lower Egypt: Sais, the Delta and Memphis

ledger.note: 712: Shebitku brings the whole Nile Valley under direct Kushite rule. The 25th Dynasty page says he conquered the whole Nile Valley "around 712 BC" and had Bocchoris burned to death (the Greek name of Bakenranef, whom the 24th page says Shebitqo burned alive; the identification is the researcher's); the Piye page has him defeating Bakenranef at Sais "in his second regnal year". The Twenty-fourth Dynasty page dates Bakenranef's deposition to 720; two pages and the revised chronology give about 712.
712: the Delta kings cease to be vassals when Shebitku takes the Delta directly (see the gain above).

712: the Kushite court moves its Egyptian capital to Memphis. The page says Shebitku moved the capital to Memphis after conquering Lower Egypt; another passage gives the move to Shabaka ("transferred the capital to Memphis"), so the conquest year is used.

671: Esarhaddon invades the Delta. A first attempt in 673-674 was beaten back ("Taharqa and his army defeated the Assyrians outright in 674", Babylonian records); in 671 he took Memphis and installed Necho I at Sais (Assyrian conquest page). The war runs to 663.

region.text: Lower Egypt: Memphis and the Delta

ledger.note: 671: Memphis falls to Esarhaddon and Taharqa flees south. The Assyrian conquest page lists Lower Egypt and Taharqa's family as lost to Esarhaddon in 671.
669: Taharqa retakes the north. The page says he reoccupied Memphis and the Delta and the Assyrian governors fled; Esarhaddon died on the way to a new campaign.

region.text: Lower Egypt: Memphis and the Delta

ledger.note: 667: Ashurbanipal drives Taharqa out of the north. The page says Ashurbanipal defeated Taharqa, who fled to Thebes, and his army advanced as far south as Thebes, though the 25th page adds that direct Assyrian control was not established. The Delta is drawn as lost; Necho I was reinstated as vassal about 665.

region.text: the Nile Valley as far as Memphis

ledger.note: 664: Tantamani recovers Memphis. The 25th page says he sailed north to Thebes, was ritually installed and regained Egypt as far as Memphis, killing Necho I; the Assyrian conquest page narrates the same return under 663.

region.text: Lower Egypt: Memphis and the Delta

ledger.note: 663: Thebes is sacked and the north is lost for good. Psamtik I's army fought Tantamani near Memphis, Tantamani fled upriver and Thebes was sacked (Assyrian conquest page; the 25th page also gives 663). The Third Intermediate Period page says the Assyrians delivered a mortal blow, "sacking Thebes", in 664.
663: the Assyrian war ends in an Assyrian victory (infobox); Kushite authority in Upper Egypt persisted until 656.

656: Psamtik I takes Thebes without a fight. The 25th page says his fleet peacefully took control of Upper Egypt, ending Kushite rule; "Thebes peacefully submitted itself to Psamtik's fleet in 656 BC" (Third Intermediate Period page). [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Counterpart changed from twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt to assyrian-egypt: Psamtik I was still Assyria's vassal king in 656 (assyrian-egypt, 664-655, gains Thebes in 656); the 26th Dynasty dossier begins in 655.

region.text: Upper Egypt, the dynasty's last holding

ledger.note: 656: the Kushite dynasty ends in Egypt. The infobox says Disestablished 656 BC; "The 25th Dynasty ended with its rulers retreating to their spiritual homeland at Napata" (Third Intermediate Period page), where the Kingdom of Kush goes on. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Counterpart changed from twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt to assyrian-egypt: Psamtik I was still Assyria's vassal king in 656 (assyrian-egypt, 664-655, gains Thebes in 656); the 26th Dynasty dossier begins in 655.

wars.name: Piye's invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: Piye won at Herakleopolis, took Hermopolis and Memphis and received the submission of the Delta kings, then returned to Nubia without garrisoning the Delta.
wars.note: Date from the Victory Stele page (year 20 of a reign from about 747); other pages give 732 and 725.

wars.name: Shebitku's conquest of the Delta
wars.outcome: Shebitku took Sais, captured Bakenranef and ruled the whole valley; the capital moved to Memphis.
wars.note: Piye page: "in his second regnal year"; 25th page: "around 712 BC". The 24th Dynasty page says 720.

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Esarhaddon took Memphis in 671, Taharqa returned in 669, Ashurbanipal drove him to Thebes in 667, Tantamani's return of 664/663 ended with the sack of Thebes; Psamtik I, the Assyrian vassal, unified the north.
wars.note: Infobox territorial change: "vassalised Egypt for a period of about 10 years". The failed raid of 673 is dated 674 in Babylonian records.

wars.name: Sennacherib's campaign in Judah (Eltekeh)
wars.outcome: Taharqa's army aided Hezekiah; it was "beaten at Eltekeh", though the page says it "could be interpreted as a victory for the double kingdom". No Egyptian land changed hands.

wars.name: Revolt of Ashdod
wars.outcome: The page says Shabaka backed an uprising at Ashdod, which Sargon II defeated; the rebel Iamani was extradited to Assyria in 712. No border moved.

certainty.note: The pages name cities and rulers, not frontiers; the Delta kings and Memphis change hands several times. No treaty line exists in the period.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for the Kushite dynasty as rule over Egypt; its Kingdom of Kush shape for -700..-676 (563,237 km2) is Nubia plus all Egypt, and the Twenty-second and Twenty-third Dynasty rows for -800..-701 are reviewed by me-03-b as wrong. This dossier draws only the Egyptian realm; Nubia stays with kingdom-of-kush (af-01), whose ledger already records the same Egyptian gains and losses with the Twenty-second Dynasty or neo-assyrian-empire as counterpart. The two dossiers should not both be drawn over Egypt in the same colour; the colour agent should give the Egyptian realm the egypt family.

Dates the pages dispute: the dynasty begins 754 (infobox), 747 (body) or 744 (lead, Piye page); Piye's campaign is c. 732 (Third Intermediate Period page), about 728 (Victory Stele page, from the reign start 747) or about 725 (Piye page, from 744); Shebitku's conquest of the Delta is "around 712" (25th page, Piye page) against Bakenranef's deposition in 720 (24th Dynasty page); Thebes is sacked in 664 (Third IP page) or 663 (Assyrian page, 25th page). The choices are named in each note. The 25th page gives no area; Kashta's real control of Thebes is doubted by the page itself.

Gazetteer: no name needed; Herakleopolis and Hermopolis are drawn through the Upper Egypt, Lower Egypt and Fayyum regions. The Kushite hold on the Levantine coast (Gaza, Ashdod in 720-712) is not drawn: the pages record revolts that Assyria crushed, not territory.
